content.thinking:
I'm looking at the incident: metrics went dark after deploy P2 renamed the metrics port from "metrics" to "http-metrics," while the logs show the service still serving at about the same error and disconnect rates as before.

I'm working through the causal chain: nobody using the shop saw a problem, but its metrics stopped being collected. The likely cause is the deploy P2 renaming the metrics port, and I'm checking whether the earlier change P1 could explain it, since metrics were still present after that one.

I've ruled out the earlier change P1: metrics were still readable with P1 in place, and rolling back to P1's revision brought them back. Flag changes are also off the table, since nobody but the automation touched them. That leaves the rename in P2 as the cause, most likely because the scrape config's selector still matches the old port name.

I'm checking whether the mechanism actually holds: the scrape config selects targets by port name, so a name nothing matches would stop collection, and restoring the old name restored metrics, but the specific scrape.yaml selector value still comes from a file read rather than a diff.

I'm settling the root cause now: the scrape selects targets by port name, and the deploy renamed the port while the scrape selector was left alone, so the scraper matched nothing even as the shop kept serving.

I'm settling on the chain now: the deploy at P2 changed the metrics port name from "metrics" to "http-metrics," and the scrape configuration was left selecting the old name, so the scraper found no target.

I'm settling the mechanism now: the deploy renamed the shop's metrics port in the production values file, and the scrape configuration, which the deploy left alone, selects its target by that name, so it no longer matches anything.

I'm listing the contributing factors now, starting with the missing check: nothing seems to confirm that the port name in the values file matches what the scrape configuration selects, and a check there would have caught the rename before it shipped. I'm also weighing which follow-up item should address it, leaning toward a consistency check run in the pre-merge pipeline for every change like this one.

I'm now considering whether nobody was paged, since the MetricsAbsent alert links to no on-call, and wondering if that would have shortened the incident.

I'm weighing whether the alert's delay is itself a contributing factor, since the record doesn't show what accounted for the rest of the time before it fired. I'll keep that question open rather than assume it.

I'm drafting a contributing factor on the alert's delay: the record doesn't show what took the extra time beyond the evaluation and scrape allowance, so I'd propose an item to find and remove it. I'm also considering a third factor, that no post-deploy check confirmed the scraper still had a target for the shop, which would have caught the rollout.

I'm drafting the action items: a pre-merge check on the port name, a post-deploy check that the shop still has a scrape target, and an investigation into the alert's delay. I'm also noting the paging gap as a process item. Next, I'm starting on the lessons, beginning with what went well: the rollback and the link from the stop to the deploy.

I'm going through the remaining sections of the review: a went-wrong note that nobody was paged, and a list of assumptions I'm still checking, like the rollback confirmation and the scrape selector that I only have through a file read.

I'm settling how the still-at-risk note should read: any deploy of what the repository now holds could stop the shop's metrics again, and a rename of the port in one of the two files but not the other could do the same at any time.

I'm settling the root cause in plain terms: the scrape configuration finds the shop's metrics endpoint by port name rather than number, and the deploy changed that name in the production values file without touching the scrape configuration, so the scraper had nothing to collect from.

I'm checking the chain's first step: the shop's users saw nothing wrong, and what showed up instead was its metrics no longer arriving. I'm also confirming the earlier revision isn't the source, since its metrics were readable and the timing doesn't point to it.

I'm drafting the went-well list now, starting with the rollback, which the Mitigation Agent carried out on the deployment after confirming the metrics could be read again. Next I'm checking how the Investigator Agent tied the stop to what the deployment changed, then noting that the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request.

Still drafting the went-well list, checking the PR link for the Code-Fix proposal.

action_items.item: Add a required pre-merge check, run on every change to the deploy/ directory, that fails when metrics.portName in deploy/values-production.yaml differs from any port name the scrape configuration selects.
Add a post-deploy check to io-shop's rollout that fails the rollout when the scraper has no target for the shop.
Find out what took the {beyond_accounted_for} by which the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop came later than its evaluation and scrape allowance account for, and remove it.
Route MetricsAbsent alerts on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when they fire.

causal_chain.step: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. What was seen instead was that the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and the monitoring went blind to the service.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9: the shop's metrics were still being collected with it in place up to the minute before the onset, and they could be read again once the rollback put that revision back.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before it was read.

causal_chain.step: The metrics stopped because of the deploy recorded at {P2.1}, which changed metrics.portName from metrics to http-metrics in deploy/values-production.yaml. That was the only change in the deploy.
The rename stopped collection because the deploy left the scrape configuration unchanged, so the scrape no longer matched any port on the shop and had no target to collect from.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, but the monitoring was not changed to use the new label, so it stopped collecting them.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that makes the port name in deploy/values-production.yaml agree with the name the scrape configuration selects. The values file's own comment says the name carries weight and that a name nothing matches stops collection without any error.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The rename would have been caught before it merged, and the scrape would never have lost its target.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen after rollout that the scraper still had a target for the shop, so the deploy finished even though collection had stopped.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The rollout would have flagged or halted the deploy right away, rather than the loss being found only when the absent-metrics alert fired.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The absent-metrics alert came {beyond_accounted_for} later than its evaluation interval and scrape allowance account for, and the record does not show what took that time.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The alert would have fired sooner, and the stretch the metrics did not cover would have been shorter.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read what the deploy of 9f4ad14 changed and found the one-line rename of the metrics port name.
The Mitigation Agent rolled io-shop back off revision 9f4ad14, and the rollback can be undone.
The Mitigation Agent checked that the service's metrics could be read again before judging the rollback confirmed.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/537 for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the MetricsAbsent alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called in while the shop's metrics were missing.

input.root_cause: The scrape configuration picks the shop's metrics endpoint by the port's name rather than its number, and the deploy renamed that port from metrics to http-metrics in deploy/values-production.yaml without changing the scrape configuration, which it left as it was. The scraper's selector then matched no port and it had nothing to collect from, while nothing reported an error.
input.still_at_risk: Any deploy of what the repository now holds could stop the shop's metrics again, and any later rename of the port in one deploy file but not the other could do the same.
input.symptom: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped being collected
